title: Phở Bò
description: A clear, deeply beefy broth perfumed with charred onion, ginger, star anise, and cinnamon, ladled boiling over rice noodles and raw sirloin.
notes: The broth freezes perfectly. Ask the butcher to cut the bones into short lengths so the marrow is exposed.

steps.text: Cover the beef bones with cold water, boil hard for five minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and the pot.
steps.tip: Parboiling removes the scum that would cloud the broth. Skipping it is the usual reason homemade phở is murky.

steps.text: Char the onions and ginger directly over a flame or under the grill until blackened in patches.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, whole cloves, coriander seeds, and black cardamom in a dry pan until fragrant, then tie them in muslin.
Return the bones to the pot with the 5 L of water, the brisket, and the charred onions and ginger. Bring to a bare simmer and skim.
Add the spice bag and simmer gently, uncovered, skimming now and then. Lift out the brisket when tender, after about 90 minutes, and chill it.
Strain the broth and season with the fish sauce, rock sugar, and salt.
steps.tip: It should taste slightly too salty on its own. The noodles take it down.

steps.text: Soak or blanch the rice noodles and divide between deep bowls. Top with thin slices of the cooked brisket and the raw sirloin, fanned out.
Bring the broth to a rolling boil and ladle it over, so it cooks the sirloin pink. Scatter with the white onion and green onions.
steps.tip: Boiling, not merely hot — or the raw beef stays raw.

steps.text: Serve with a plate of Thai basil, cilantro, bean sprouts, limes, and chillies, with hoisin sauce and sriracha on the table.
